name: Republic of China (Taiwan)

areaKm2.note: CIA Factbook: total 35,980 km2 incl. Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu; land 32,260 km2 (low). High is MOI's 36,197 km2 figure (educated recollection).

population.note: Ministry of the Interior household registration, end-June 2026: 23,243,565 (down 103,176 year on year; 30th consecutive monthly decline). Not in World Bank data.

urbanization.note: CIA Factbook: 80.1% urban (2023). Not in World Bank data.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.309-310 as quoted: 170,600 active (CIA Factbook 2025 ~170,000; IISS 2024: 150,000-169,000). ROC Armed Forces article infobox (Taipei Times, 2026): 230,000 incl. 1-year conscripts (high). Coast Guard Administration (11,800 paramilitary) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 1,657,000 reserves. Low is an educated figure for reservists actually organised in units with recent call-up training (annual ~14-day training reaches far fewer).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 170,600 minus infantry P roles 54,000 = 116,600. Navy (~40,000 incl. marines counted above), Air Force (~35,000 per IISS 2023), artillery/armour crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Universal male conscription (1 year from 2024) and 1.66 million listed reservists; whole-of-society resilience plans. 7% is ~1.6 million.

count.note: Educated guess. Army ~94,000 in combined-arms brigades; 1-year conscripts from 2024 boost infantry battalions. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Republic_of_China_Army)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: trained staff and US-assisted reforms (Han Kuang exercises now unscripted), but no combat since 1958 and contested doctrine (asymmetric vs legacy).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: national conscript/volunteer mix; recruitment shortfalls.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: existential defence of the island; polls show majority willingness to fight.

weapons.note: Anchor 9-10: Hsiung Feng III, HIMARS, Harpoon, ATACMS, drone programmes.

ships.note: Anchor 9: old hulls with modern missiles; Tuo Chiang corvettes; Hai Kun on trial.

fortification.note: Anchor 10 minus: hardened underground air bases (Chiashan), Patriot/TK-III layered defence, beach obstacles.

logistics.note: Anchor 9: dense island infrastructure, energy import vulnerability (LNG ~11 days).

communications.note: Anchor 9-10: Link-16, hardened networks; undersea-cable cuts a risk.

isr.note: Anchor 9: E-2K, long-range early-warning radar (Leshan), MQ-9B arriving.

air.note: Anchor 9 plus: F-16V (4.5 gen) - no 5th-generation aircraft.

cyber.note: Anchor 10 minus: Information, Communications and Electronic Force Command; constant PRC cyber pressure.

gdpPerCapita.note: GDP 1,648,236,286,485 (corrected gdp mid, rebase factor 0.8306) / population 23,243,565 (MOI June 2026) = 70,912. Range +/-15%. Cross-check: IMF PPP per capita ~$80,000+ current int$ in 2025 (not fetched). Audit 2026-10-29: corrected from 68,339 (58,088-78,590), which still used the old 0.8005 rebase factor after gdp had been corrected, so gdp != population x gdpPerCapita.

gdp.note: Not in World Bank data. CIA Factbook real GDP (PPP) 2023 $1.743 trillion (Factbook constant-dollar series) x 1.048 (2024 growth, educated from DGBAS releases not fetched) x 1.0863 (DGBAS 2025 growth 8.63%, Focus Taiwan 30 Jan 2026: https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202601300021) x 0.8005 (2021->2011 rebase) = 1,588,436,235,112 2011 int$. Range +/-15%. Source page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/east-n-southeast-asia/tw.json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: ROC Armed Forces article: 2026 budget 'greater than 3% of GDP for the first time since 2009' (US$20.1 billion infobox); CIA Factbook 2.4% (2024) as low. Not in World Bank/SIPRI-WB data.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. DGBAS industry share (not fetched) is ~35-40% and rose with the 2024-25 AI/semiconductor export boom. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/east-n-southeast-asia/tw.json)

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Floored at 0 (field cannot be negative): calorie self-sufficiency ~30-35%; dependent on grain imports - blockade vulnerability.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Males turning 18: births in 2007-2008 were ~200,000 per year (MOI, not fetched) x ~52% male. Falls sharply after 2030 (2025 births ~107,000). (context page: https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/news/6398792)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. CM32/CM34 Clouded Leopard line. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Republic_of_China_Army)

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. AIDC upgrade/assembly capacity; no current new-build fighter line. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_Air_Force)

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Lung Teh/Jong Shyn yards (Tuo Chiang corvettes, Kuang Hua). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Republic_of_China_Navy_ships)

submarines.note: Educated guess. CSBC Hai Kun programme. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Republic_of_China_Navy_ships)

missiles.note: Educated guess. NCSIST Hsiung Feng/Tien Kung launchers. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Republic_of_China_Navy_ships)

drones.note: Educated guess. Group 2+ incl. civilian drone industry conversion. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Republic_of_China_Army)

roadKm.note: asOf 2019: 41,475 km total (list as quoted, paved figure 42,793 km is inconsistent and used as high); 1,053 km expressway.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 1,613 km (2018) incl. 345 km high-speed; 150 km industrial 762 mm lines excluded.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 8 ports, 1 large (Kaohsiung) + 3 medium = 4; key ports Keelung, Hualien, Kaohsiung, Su-ao; high adds Taichung and Taipei.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 5,901 thousand DWT under the national flag. Range +/-10%. 465 ships (Factbook 2023); Taiwanese owners (Evergreen, Yang Ming) operate far more under foreign flags.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Island defence on interior lines; no expeditionary capacity.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists nine nuclear-armed states; Taiwan is not one of them.

basesAbroad.name: Taiping Island (Itu Aba), Spratlys - ROC garrison

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: fortified island with mountainous interior, few suitable landing beaches, monsoon/typhoon seasons that restrict invasion windows, strong population support.

notes: Modern snapshot asOf mid-2026. Taiwan is not in World Bank data: population from the Ministry of the Interior (June 2026), GDP from the CIA Factbook PPP series rolled forward with DGBAS growth (grade C), urbanisation/area/rail/ports from the CIA Factbook. Population convention: Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu (ne:TWN polygon may not include Kinmen/Matsu). Doctrine: archetype-modern-small-state, because the doctrine profile names Taiwan's newer whole-of-society/asymmetric concept explicitly, although Taiwan's force is larger than most small states. Counts from Wikipedia ROC Army equipment list (IISS 2024/2026 as quoted for several lines), ROC Navy ship list, ROCAF article; fighter count is a composite (grade C). Personnel sources disagree (IISS 170,600 vs 230,000 incl. conscripts). US weapons backlog (F-16 Block 70, Harpoon CDS, MQ-9B) means 2026-27 strength will rise.
